title: Free Fall and Newton's Second Law
learningObjectives: Describe free-falling motion as motion under only the gravitational force and apply a=F_net/m to predict the acceleration.
Interpret how constant acceleration produces linear growth in velocity and quadratic growth in displacement, and recognize that drag adds an extra force in air.

explanations.text: An object falling through a vacuum experiences only the gravitational force as the net force, and its free-fall motion is governed by Newton's second law which links net force and mass to acceleration.

evidence.quote: An object that falls through a vacuum is subjected to only one external force, the gravitational force, expressed as the weight of the object.
is said to be free falling and its motion is described by Newton’s second law of motion.

explanations.text: In ideal free-fall the acceleration is constant at the value g, so objects of different size and mass accelerate equally when drag is absent.

evidence.quote: The acceleration is constant and equal to the gravitational acceleration g which is 9.8 meters per square second at sea level on the Earth.
In a vacuum, a beach ball falls with the same acceleration as an airliner.

explanations.text: Constant acceleration causes velocity to increase linearly with time and position to increase quadratically, while motion through the atmosphere involves an additional drag force that makes the description more complex.

evidence.quote: Notice that the acceleration is a constant, the velocity increases linearly, and the location increases quadratically.
If the object falls through the atmosphere, there is an additional drag force acting on the object
